September 15, 2026

Supreme Court declines to revive Trump mail-in ballot restrictions

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

The Supreme Court denied the Trump administration's request to pause a preliminary injunction issued by a federal judge in Massachusetts that blocks the government from using an executive order to restrict mail-in voting. The ruling was reported as 7-2, with Justices Alito and Thomas dissenting and Justice Kavanaugh concurring. The order leaves the restrictions blocked for now, making it unlikely they take effect before the midterm elections.

ICE agents accused of beating two US citizen teenagers headed to enlist

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Two teenage U.S. citizens said they were pepper-sprayed, pulled from a vehicle and punched by ICE agents while on their way to file enlistment paperwork with the Marines, according to video first obtained by Telemundo. The teens had been filming agents arresting parents outside Santos Livas Elementary School in Alamo, Texas, and were detained for nearly eight hours before release. One of them, Luis Ochoa, said he told agents he was a U.S. citizen and an agent replied, "I don't give a damn. Your parents can't help you now." The mother of one teenager said she no longer knows whether they will serve in the military.

Congress opens investigation into Russian oligarch funding of Don Jr wedding

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Representative Robert Garcia and the House Oversight Committee announced an investigation into reports that a Kremlin-linked Russian oligarch paid for parts of Donald Trump Jr's wedding to Bettina Anderson, which the couple confirmed receiving. Melania Trump said in a statement that she has never had a relationship with the man and played no role in organizing the event, while Eric Trump and the president both said they do not know who he is. Trump did not attend the wedding, citing the military conflict with Iran.

Trump blames Biden for price increases as oil stays elevated

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Trump posted that price increases throughout America were caused by Joe Biden and his administration rather than by his own, adding that oil was higher under Biden than it is now and that his administration prevented Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. He said that with the temporary exception of oil, prices are coming down sharply, and that oil will fall once the military conflict with Iran ends. The post came roughly 600 days into his second term.

Costco rations motor oil as mortgage rates and yields climb

tags: economy, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Costco has begun rationing parts of its Kirkland Signature motor oil line and raising prices, with a pack that once cost about $30 now costing about $58 and members limited to two units every seven days, as supplies of premium base oils remain squeezed in response to the Iran war. Mortgage interest rates have risen above 7% and the 10-year Treasury note yield has passed 5%, the highest since July 2007. Gas and diesel prices continue to rise.

Trump defends AI and data centers in repeated posts and podcast call-in

tags: tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump posted at least three times about artificial intelligence and the importance of data centers, dismissing warnings that AI could end humanity as fake news. He then called into a live taping of the All-In podcast, where NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang was a guest, to repeat that AI poses no danger to society. CNN reported that some inside the White House are concerned he is downplaying the risks too heavily.

Musk-funded voter site accused of harvesting personal data and giving wrong answers

tags: politics, privacy
sources: @carolinegleich, @total.hypocrisy

A website called VoteSafe, run by Elon Musk's super PAC America PAC, collects users' names, dates of birth, home addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and location while tracking clicks and page views, with a privacy policy that permits selling that information, including registration status and inferred "psychological trends" and "aptitude," to business partners. Because it checks registration against America PAC's own voter list rather than official state records, the site can tell users they are registered when their county says otherwise. The PAC has spent more than $180,000 in a single week promoting the site on Facebook and Instagram. Voters were urged to use vote.org or official state records instead.

Speaker Johnson pours cold water on promised $5,000 checks

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

House Speaker Mike Johnson said the $5,000 payments Trump has promised if Republicans win the midterms would take a long time and are essentially just ideas. There is not currently enough support within the Republican caucus to approve payments of that size to every American, even if the party retains its House and Senate majorities. Earlier proposals for DOGE checks and tariff dividend checks were never delivered.

Anthropic says Claude was used to build military targeting material

tags: tech, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Anthropic said its Claude model was used to build targeting handbooks naming U.S. Navy sailors. Separately, a cell in Yemen used the model to develop guided-weapons software and returned to it after a failed rocket test.

Air commander says bases held bomb bodies they could not use in Iran air war

tags: defence, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

The general who ran the air campaign against Iran said bases had bomb bodies on hand that could not be used. He offered an explanation for why the munitions were unusable.

Retired pilot says some Air Force fighter pilots fly about once a month

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A retired F-16 pilot said some Air Force fighter pilots may now be flying only about once a month. He said current official flight-hour figures are no longer publicly reported.

Soldier's father detained by ICE while military parole application pending

tags: immigration, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

A woman who joined the Army filed for military parole for her father. More than a year later, Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained him while the application was still pending.

Federal judge orders Army to revisit discharge labelled a condition, not a disability

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army discharged a soldier on the basis of what it called a "condition, not a disability." A federal judge has ordered the service to review the case again, pointing to problems with the medical record at the centre of the dispute.

McConnell returns to Senate after day-long absence amid frailty concerns

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @hunteralexanderhowell

Senator Mitch McConnell remained inside his Washington home for most of Monday with Capitol Police vehicles outside and his doors and windows shuttered, while the Senate convened at 3 p.m. He was later filmed being wheeled out of the house and taken to the Capitol, where he voted and gave brief remarks outside the Senate gallery that reporters were barred from recording. Video showed him largely motionless in the vehicle with a dark spot on his hand, and observers described his speech as slowed and his appearance as increasingly frail.

Trump revives Butler shooting claims as Patel testifies in Senate

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Trump posted on the morning of September 15 that the Biden-era FBI mishandled the investigation into the Butler, Pennsylvania shooting, saying most of the information was missing, altered, corrupted or gone by the time he took office and that new information had just been found. He described the episode as a Democratic plot to remove him from the election and said former FBI director Christopher Wray should pay a price. The post came on the day FBI director Kash Patel testified before the Senate.

Scholars warn House clerk role could be used to block swearing-in of new members

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The transfer of power in a newly elected House runs through the clerk of the House of Representatives, a nominally nonpartisan officer who presides over the opening of a new Congress and the vote for speaker. Neither the Constitution nor statute explicitly bars the sitting speaker from firing the clerk and installing a replacement before that point, a question legal scholars are divided on. If a loyalist were installed, they could decline to swear in members or hold the speaker vote, pushing the dispute into the courts.

Former Trump aide and pastors push to repeal the 19th Amendment

tags: politics
sources: @carolinegleich

John McEntee, a former Trump White House aide who ran the Presidential Personnel Office and later advised Project 2025, posted a video captioned "Sorry we want MALE only voting. The 19th might have to go," later saying he meant "male" as in men. Dale Partridge, a pastor in Prescott, Arizona, announced a book titled "19 Reasons to Repeal the 19th Amendment" and said he wants women's suffrage overturned within ten years. In August 2025 the Secretary of Defense shared a CNN segment featuring pastors who said they would support repeal; the Pentagon later said he does believe women should have the right to vote. Utah women first voted in 1870 and had that right stripped by Congress in 1887, regaining it nine years later.

Intruder breaches Australian air base used by US Marines

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

An intruder allegedly breached RAAF Base Darwin, a facility used by U.S. Marines, assaulted security personnel and escaped in a stolen security vehicle. Police pursued the vehicle and lost it.

Navy orders removal of air conditioners sailors bought for barracks

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Sailors living in a Navy barracks without air conditioning bought their own units. The Navy has now ordered those units removed.

National Voter Registration Day prompts calls to check registration status

tags: politics
sources: @carolinegleich

September 15 was National Voter Registration Day, with voters urged to confirm their registration even if they have voted before. Moving, name changes, turning 18, becoming a citizen or sitting out elections can all require an update. Utah's registration deadline is October 23, with same-day in-person registration available after that.

Commentary questions whether AI risk warnings are a coordinated operation

tags: tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

A commentary argued that simultaneous warnings from figures such as Sam Altman and Elon Musk about AI destroying humanity are coordinated, pointing to a former Anthropic and OpenAI employee's television appearances and to industry executives calling for regulation as evidence of an effort to centralise control of the technology. It cited a "simulated sentience hypothesis" holding that a staged performance of rogue AI behaviour could be used to justify extraordinary government powers. It urged viewers not to ask the government to centralise anything.
